findings.title: A FIFO at hub.json hangs Fabric's quit for good; the quit deadline and reaper are never armed
findings.evidence: hub.ts:117 withdrawHub reads hub.json with readFileSync (no regular-file check, no O_NONBLOCK); index.ts:597-599 runs it as a quit stop; quit.ts:95-101 runs every stop before arming the 10 s deadline and the 15 s outside reaper. Probe p1-withdraw-fifo.mjs: a regular hub.json was withdrawn in 1 ms; with a FIFO it was still blocked at 5000 ms and was SIGKILLed. Probe p2-quit-order.mjs printed: stop, then 'deadline armed 10000ms', then 'reaper armed 15000ms'.
findings.fix: Read hub.json like agentRegistry.readRegularFile (lstat, O_NONBLOCK open, fstat isFile, bounded read), or compare a stat with the inode and startedAt kept in memory. Arm the deadline and the reaper in quit.ts before running stops. Add a FIFO-plant test.

findings.title: Every external request whose caller hangs up keeps its admission slot for ever; 32 lock out a credential, 128 close the hub
findings.evidence: agentSurface.ts:706-794 releases externalPending and externalPendingTotal only in the finally after 'await transport.handleRequest' (line 787). In JSON-response mode, MCP SDK 1.30.0 webStandardStreamableHttp.js:578-595 settles that promise only through resolveJson, and close() (771-787), which res 'close' calls at agentSurface.ts:781, never calls it. Probe p8-hangup-slot-leak.mjs: after 32 hung-up agent.calls the slots were {thisCredential:32,total:32}, and the next valid request got 429 'too many concurrent requests'. Control p8-control.mjs: a waited call releases its slot (0/0).
findings.fix: Release the slot exactly once, on res 'close' or 'finish', or in the finally (a guarded release()); alternatively race handleRequest against res 'close'. Add a test: N+1 hung-up calls, then a valid call answers 200.

findings.title: A failed live-bindings read at start (a budget hint) also takes down the session surface
findings.evidence: agentSurface.ts:343 awaits primeCredentialVerifiers() before creating any server; the fallback surface.start() in hub.ts:173-179 throws the same way. Probe p7-prime-failure.mjs: startHub returned open:false, not-started, and the session surface endpoint was '' (0.3.0 had no DB dependency here).
findings.fix: Catch the prime failure in start(), log it with ops.failed, and continue listening.

findings.title: A repeated stop after a scope change answers 'refused' although the first write may have run
findings.evidence: claudeProviderControl.ts:194 runs the scope check before the cached return at :198; codexProviderControl.ts:168 before :172. Probe p6-stop-repeat-scope.mjs: first 'outcome_unknown request_timeout', writes 1; repeat after the scope change 'refused scope_changed', writes 1.
findings.fix: Return cached or pending before the scope check, or map scope_changed to outcome_unknown once canonicalCommand is set. Test both controllers.

findings.title: A poller that hung up still consumes the one-time binding credential; later polls say it was handed over
findings.evidence: hubTools.ts:136-143 does not pass extra.signal to access.status. accessService.ts:268-275 mints the credential, appends access.credential.claimed@1 and returns it unconditionally. accessService.ts:263 then tells later polls the credential was handed over once.
findings.fix: Pass the signal, check signal.aborted inside the serial job before minting, and change the note to 'issued to the first read; if you did not receive it, ask again'.

findings.title: A POST carrying no state can end the operator's pending connect attempt
findings.evidence: productConnect.ts:306-320 deletes the single pending state on a malformed delivery before reading any state. Probe p3-callback-cancel.mjs: a stateless text/plain POST got 415 and lastOutcome became failed/invalid-delivery; the product's genuine delivery with the real state then got 400 'unknown or already used state', so the key is revoked. This is intended by the earlier V2 ER-9 test.
findings.fix: Settle an attempt only from a delivery that carries its valid state; log stateless malformed posts and do nothing else.

findings.title: Keyless agent.call has no duplicate guard, and its outcome-unknown text names a key never sent; answered keys re-send after 24 h
findings.evidence: hubCall.ts:451 forwards every keyless call; hubCall.ts:185-191 says 'this idempotencyKey is refused'; hubCall.ts:71 and :459-461 expire answered keys after 24 h (documented). Probe p5-idem.mjs: 'retry K +24h ... sent 2'; a keyless repeat after outcome-unknown reached 'sent 4'.
findings.fix: Require idempotencyKey for SENDS_MAIL capabilities (or all agent.call), and word the keyless outcome-unknown separately.

findings.title: Every fabric.access.request re-reads the whole registry synchronously, with no cap on the number of files
findings.evidence: accessService.ts:158 calls refresh() per request; agentRegistry.ts:283 and :249-268 read every file synchronously with no file-count cap; the door admits up to 600 requests/min. Probe p4-registry-cost.mjs: 20 files 0.6 ms; 1000 files 29.7 ms; 1000 x 60 KiB 57.0 ms per refresh on the main thread.
findings.fix: Cap the entry count, and debounce or mtime-gate refresh() on the request path.

findings.title: Hub database calls have no deadline, and all access writes, operator revocations included, share one serial chain
findings.evidence: index.ts:477-479 creates the Supabase client with no fetch timeout (undici defaults of about 300 s apply); accessStore.ts passes no abortSignal; accessService.ts:119-123 serializes request, status, decide and revoke. Read only; not measured with a stalled PostgREST.
findings.fix: Add a per-call abortSignal(AbortSignal.timeout(...)) in accessStore; consider letting operator acts not queue behind agent polls.
